purpose: Define and adversarially rehearse the recovery-point, recovery-time, encryption-key continuity, and post-restore activation boundary required before Mythical can claim that protected autonomous-company evidence is recoverable. The control consumes current A-051 backup/restore evidence, binds its exact compact digest and contract digest into three ordered payload-free recovery generations, encrypts the current capsule with an ephemeral AES-256-GCM key, measures fresh-point selection and local restore time against fixed synthetic objectives, simulates loss of the primary active key, requires two valid signatures from three independent ephemeral recovery approvers before reading a separate temporary recovery-key copy, verifies exact authenticated decryption, refuses insufficient, untrusted, revoked, substituted, stale, future, corrupted, wrong-key, and same-domain recovery, and checks global disable after decryption but before activation. It retains no key or capsule after the run, invokes no scheduled company workflow, grants no eligible-cycle credit, configures no provider, account, region, secret manager, key-management service, production backup, production restore, or production objective, and authorizes no network, repository, dispatch, spend, or external action.

activationGates.gate: D-017 records the operating cell, accountable backup owner, restore operator, key custodian, independent recovery approvers, backup, urgent recipient, recovery operator, kill operator, and runtime/durability/key-management classes
The exact provider, accounts, regions, failure domains, storage classes, secret manager, key-management service, support boundary, service objectives, and all-in cost are selected and approved
Separated least-privilege backup, restore, key-use, key-administration, recovery-approval, recovery-execution, kill, alert, and independent assurance identities are attested and revocable
Recovery-point and recovery-time objectives, measurement origins, clocks, exclusions, breach behavior, alert thresholds, review cadence, and customer/operational consequences are approved
Payload-free capsule, authenticated encryption, additional authenticated data, nonce, key version, generation, ordering, digest, retention, deletion, and compatibility semantics are approved

Primary and recovery key material use approved provider-native protection, rotation, revocation, recovery, escrow, access logging, hard deletion, and separation from storage and runtime administrators

Storage, primary key, recovery key, identity, approval, alert, and operator dependencies use independently reviewed failure domains with no hidden shared account, region, quota, provider, or recovery dependency
Current, predecessor, rotated, revoked, missing, wrong, corrupt, destroyed, inaccessible, and compromised key paths are deterministic, monitored, exercised, and fail closed

Recovery-key release requires the approved threshold of independently authenticated, exact-request, non-revoked approvers and cannot be self-approved by backup, restore, runtime, or key administrators

Every recovery point is independently timestamped and bound to exact evidence, generation, key version, retention and completion state; stale, future, rollback, substituted, partial, or ambiguous points cannot count as recovered
Measured RPO and RTO include detection, decision, key recovery, restore, reconciliation and ready-for-admission time, and objective breaches remain visible rather than being reclassified or excluded
Global disable, cancellation, identity/key revocation, budget stops, process-tree kill and fence checks remain enforceable during key loss, decrypt, restore, reconciliation and admission

Decryption and objective compliance cannot activate schedules, admit or execute packets, grant promotion credit, access unrelated credentials, write repositories, dispatch, spend, alert externally, or take any external action

Key loss, key corruption, secret-manager outage, administrator loss, approver loss, account/region loss, clock fault, stale point, RPO breach, RTO breach, alert loss and total restore exercises pass with measured evidence
Runtime tracing proves zero unexpected key disclosure, raw payload, contact detail, repository mutation, network, subprocess, dispatch, spend or external effect across the complete recovery matrix

Independent open-world evaluation covers cryptographic misuse, parser differential, nonce reuse, downgrade, rollback, compromised approver, key oracle, recovery poisoning, denial of service, and objective gaming
Four accurate independently reviewed protected cycles include measured RPO/RTO and at least one isolated primary-key-loss recovery with complete reconciliation and zero ambiguous success

Separate expiring approval admits the exact provider, regions, identities, approvers, keys, algorithms, generations, objectives, evidence digests, restore, reconciliation, disable, kill and alert policies
